question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
trigger: User asks for harsh honest feedback on the proposal to redesign Plite extensions into a shared plugin contract, rename the vocabulary and remove the Plate-to-Plite adapter. This is a fresh adversarial review of the immediately prior Pursue verdict. Review only.
requirements: Reconsider the latest Pursue verdict rather than treating it as settled; distinguish evidence from architectural inference.
Run the hard-cut counterfactual against the Plate authoring compiler, Plite runtime descriptor, adapter translation, public identity and proposed plugin vocabulary.
Preserve Plate product jobs: per-editor terminal configuration, ordered prior-stage inference, schema-derived capabilities, product stores/codecs/rendering and mounted-view behavior.

Preserve Plite substrate laws: independently useful raw descriptors, immutable normalized runtime definitions, candidate rollback, exact-view portals and no product configuration grammar without a raw caller job.
Identify the smallest credible deletion target and the decisive evidence needed before renaming public APIs.
Record one honest verdict and one next investigation without implementing product code or claiming unmeasured type/runtime gains.
evidenceReuse: The immediately prior review and September 12 implementation receipts were reused as hypotheses and historical context only. Rechecked the Plate authoring resolver, runtime lowerer, descriptor metadata/alias machinery, Plite extension contract and contribution tests, current Vision ownership, and representative authoring assertions. Counted unique in-source authoring call-site files only as scale context. No external discovery, runtime replay, type benchmark or prototype was executed.
summary: Defer the shared composition-engine redesign and any extension-to-plugin rename. The prior Pursue verdict overclaimed: constructing a normalized Plite descriptor proves a lowering boundary, not a duplicate plugin engine. Plate has an independent product authoring/compiler job that should not move into Plite merely to erase an adapter noun. The credible cut is narrower: retain Plate compilation while prototyping one public nominal identity and one installed portal, deleting synthetic extension references, alias/topology remapping and late cross-contract dispatch. If that prototype cannot remove the machinery without a replacement map, public compiler graph or type-cost regression, keep layer-specific plugin/extension vocabulary over the shared installed owner.
alternatives: Rename extension to plugin on the current machinery: stop; it implies unification while keeping the same translation and two descriptor meanings.
Move Plate ordered authoring, terminal configuration, product stores/schema/rendering and compilation into Plite: stop; current raw consumers do not earn that substrate and type-system cost.
Delete Plate lowering entirely: stop; product declarations still need editor-local normalization into Plite runtime capabilities.

Keep the current compiler plus every alias/reference/topology map: viable fallback, but synthetic extension references, name-based dependency remapping and cross-contract dispatch remain credible debt.

Keep Plate product compilation while sharing one public nominal descriptor identity and installed portal: strongest candidate; defer until a bounded vertical prototype demonstrates net deletion and preserves all lifetimes.
Restore distinct Plate plugin and Plite extension accessors over one installed owner: honest fallback if shared identity fails, because the authoring contracts remain semantically distinct.
proofLimits: Bounded source and assertion inspection only. The review did not build the proposed identity model, run tests, measure TypeScript declaration/type-instantiation cost, replay publication/rollback, or benchmark runtime construction/configuration. The next investigation must implement a disposable raw Plite capability, configured headless Plate plugin and React Plate plugin on one public identity; preserve inference, dependency/conflict semantics, configuration precedence, schema behavior, independent editor stores, failed-candidate rollback, exact-view behavior and static/SSR isolation; and show an actual deletion inventory. A new compiled-descriptor family, metadata bag, alias registry or public compiler graph that merely replaces the old mapping fails the experiment. Current adoption/proof fields still describe the implemented September 12 contract, not this candidate.
